summary: Classify 7 enabler-chain light/medium entities for the #428 flat-family JSON migration

result.summary: ReligionInfo (Sources/Infos/CvReligionInfo.{h,cpp}) is a CvHotkeyInfo subclass. Its real gameplay payload is THREE per-commerce tables, all of which the first-pass mapping mis-scoped. (1) StateReligionCommerces: mapping says "player" but the live consumer (CvCity.cpp:12503, `if isHasReligion(eReligion)`) deposits it in EVERY city that HAS this religion present -> commerce, CITY scope, flat. (2) HolyCityCommerces: deposits only in this religion's holy city (CvCity.cpp:12507) -> commerce, CITY scope, flat (mapping correct). (3) GlobalReligionCommerces: mapping says "player" but it is NOT per-player — it is the religion's contribution to its "shrine": consumed wherever a building's getGlobalReligionCommerce() points at this religion (CvCity.cpp:12185/12288), the per-commerce value scaled by GC.getGame().countReligionLevels (a WORLD-wide tally across all players). The value LANDS in the city holding the shrine building, so scope=city, but its magnitude is world-scaled and building-gated — flagged in notes/openQuestions. All three are flat per-commerce int tables keyed gold/research/culture/espionage (engine.COMMERCES). TechPrereq is the founding gate (CvTeam.cpp:5339 founds the religion when the tech is discovered) -> a prereq field that the store INVERTS to tech.enables; this religion IS an enabler-chain member (isEnablerChain=true), so I drop TechPrereq from the authored object. FreeUnit + iFreeUnits are a one-shot award to the founder (CvPlayer.cpp:8838-8846) -> grants. iSpreadFactor is a per-religion spread-decay scalar (CvCity.cpp:16736/16796) -> identity config. Flavors -> ai. Adjective/AdjectiveKey + Description/Civilopedia -> text. TechButton/GenericTechButton/Button/MovieFile/MovieSound/Sound/iTGAIndex -> art. m_iMissionType and m_iChar/m_iHolyCityChar are runtime-assigned (setMissionType/setChar), NOT XML-backed -> drop. m_shrineBuildings is a DERIVED runtime reverse-index (buildings with HolyCity set call addShrineBuilding at load, CvBuildingInfo.cpp:1464) -> store-derived, not authored. PropertyManipulators -> per-PROPERTY_* property family (shared CvPropertyManipulators infra). INBOUND BOOST: BuildingInfo.ReligionChanges (IDValueMap<ReligionTypes,int>, the ONLY per-specific-religion-keyed table in the codebase) is a per-religion "religion influence"/spread-weight deposit in the building's city (CvCity.cpp:4695 changeReligionInfluence) — the cascade spec (building-cascade-conversion.md:788) explicitly rules this INVERTS onto CvReligionInfo. Note: the many StateReligion* fields on Civics/Traits/Buildings (StateReligionHappiness, StateReligionGreatPeopleRateModifier, etc.) target the ABSTRACT "state religion" concept, NOT a specific ReligionInfo, so they do NOT fold onto any individual religion.

ownFields.notes: SPLIT family (gold/research/culture/espionage = engine.COMMERCES). Mapping said scope=player — WRONG. Live consumer CvCity.cpp:12503 deposits in EVERY city that isHasReligion(thisReligion); conditional on religion-presence, per-city => CITY scope. Raw per-commerce int (engine multiplies into x100 paths downstream); carry faithfully per #432.
SPLIT family. Deposits only in this religion's holy city (CvCity.cpp:12507, isHolyCity). CITY scope (mapping correct). Raw per-commerce int.

SPLIT family. Mapping said scope=player — WRONG, it is NOT per-player. This is the religion's SHRINE contribution: consumed in whichever city holds a building whose getGlobalReligionCommerce() == thisReligion (CvCity.cpp:12185/12288), the per-commerce value multiplied by countReligionLevels (WORLD-wide religion tally). Value LANDS in the shrine city => city scope, but building-gated and world-scaled. See openQuestions: the curator may need a distinct 'shrine'/world-scaled commerce family rather than plain city commerce.

Founding gate (CvTeam.cpp:5339 founds religion when tech discovered; also CvUnit.cpp:8465 prophet, CvPlayer.cpp:8795). PREREQ field -> store INVERTS to tech.enables; dropped from the authored object per curate_common cfg.drop. This religion IS an enabler-chain member (isEnablerChain=true).

Delayed-resolution UNIT_* FK (m_iFreeUnit). With iFreeUnits, one-shot award to the founding player when the religion is founded (CvPlayer.cpp:8838-8846). -> grants (e.g. grants.freeUnit + grants.numFreeUnits).
Count of FreeUnit awarded on founding (CvPlayer.cpp:8838/8844). Pairs with FreeUnit as the one-shot grant. Mapping listed under identity — WRONG, it is a grant quantity.

Per-religion spread decay/randomization scalar (CvCity.cpp:16736 decay = spreadFactor + iExp*iExp; 16796 max(1,spreadFactor) spread threshold). Religion's own config property, not a scoped modifier deposit -> identity.
AI flavour values (m_piFlavorValue, SetVariableListTagPair). -> ai group (flavours).
AdjectiveKey (CvWString m_szAdjectiveKey). Display/text key used in vote-source and event text (CvGame.cpp:9228, CvPlayer.cpp:21250). -> text.
Inherited display text key.
Inherited civilopedia text key.
Stable identifier; curate_common always drops Type from the authored body (it is the record key).
Required-read icon path (m_szTechButton; read() uses GetChildXmlValByName, the only required string). -> art.
Inherited hotkey-info button icon; getButtonDisabled derives the _D.dds variant at runtime (CvReligionInfo.cpp:151) — derived, not a separate field.
Font/TGA glyph index; feeds runtime m_iChar/m_iHolyCityChar (setChar = 8550 + tgaIndex*2). ctor default -1 is the never-read TGA-filler sentinel (RemoveTGAFiller). Art/glyph indexing.

m_aiCategories (vector<int>). isCategory()/getCategory() are generic info-category tags (no Religion-specific consumer found; same pattern as Bonus/Building categories). -> identity (classification tags).

Shared CvPropertyManipulators (m_PropertyManipulators). Splits to per-PROPERTY_* family. Handled by the common property-family path, not a religion-specific field. unit/scope follow the manipulator's own source/decay shape.
m_iMissionType is RUNTIME-assigned via setMissionType(), NOT XML-backed (confirmed CvReligionInfo.cpp:259-260). Not in getDataMembers. drop.
m_iChar/m_iHolyCityChar runtime-derived from tgaIndex (setChar/setHolyCityChar), not XML-backed. drop.

m_shrineBuildings is a DERIVED runtime reverse-index: buildings with HolyCity set push themselves in via addShrineBuilding at load (CvBuildingInfo.cpp:1464). Store-derived, NOT authored. Confirms the religion is a TARGET of BuildingInfo.HolyCity/ReligionType (the shrine relationship).

inboundBoosts.notes: The ONLY per-specific-religion-keyed table in the codebase (IDValueMap<ReligionTypes,int> m_religionChange, CvBuildingInfo.h:767). Consumer CvCity.cpp:4695 changeReligionInfluence(pair.first, pair.second*iChange) — a building deposits spread/influence weight for a SPECIFIC religion in its city. The cascade spec (Sources/docs/plans/building-cascade-conversion.md:788) explicitly mandates: 'ReligionChanges -> INVERT to CvReligionInfo (conditioner rule).' Folds onto THIS religion keyed by source building: <family>.city.buildings.<BUILDING>.flat. Family name 'religionInfluence' (spread weight) is provisional — see openQuestions; confirm against the universal singleton-family vocabulary.

openQuestions: GlobalReligionCommerces scope: the value LANDS in the shrine city (=> city scope) but is gated by a building owning getGlobalReligionCommerce()==thisReligion AND multiplied by countReligionLevels (a WORLD-wide tally). Is the right model a plain commerce.city family, or a distinct world-scaled 'shrine commerce' family? It is semantically a city deposit whose magnitude scales with a world count — the curator needs an owner ruling on whether to encode the world-scaling multiplier or treat it as opaque shrine commerce. The mapping's 'player' scope is definitely wrong either way.

Inbound-boost family name for BuildingInfo.ReligionChanges: changeReligionInfluence is religion-spread weight, not a yield/commerce/happiness. Provisionally named 'religionInfluence' (singleton family, no member). Confirm the canonical family key in the universal singleton-family list (there may already be a 'spread'/'influence' family from Civic/Trait spread-modifier consumers).

StateReligion* fields on Civics/Traits/Buildings (StateReligionHappiness, StateReligionGreatPeopleRateModifier, StateReligionUnitProductionModifier, StateReligionFreeExperience, StateReligionBuildingCommerce, etc.) target the ABSTRACT 'state religion' role, NOT a specific ReligionInfo — confirmed they fold onto the SOURCE (player-scope state-religion modifiers), NOT onto any individual religion. Listed here so a later pass does not mistakenly invert them onto ReligionInfo.

Categories: no Religion-specific consumer of isCategory/getCategory was found (only the generic info-category pattern shared with Bonus/Building). Confirm whether religion categories are read anywhere gameplay-relevant or are purely organizational identity tags.

iTGAIndex / glyph chars: classified as art/glyph indexing. Confirm the curator's art group handles a font-index int (vs a path string); the runtime m_iChar derivation lives in C++ and is not authored.

result.summary: RouteInfo is a small, mostly-static plot-feature entity: a route deposits movement cost + (optionally) tile yields onto the plot it occupies, ranks itself via iValue, and is itself GATED by a prerequisite bonus / OR-bonus list (so it is a DEPENDENT in the bonus->route enabler chain, never an enabler key — store.enabled_by("ROUTE_*") is empty, so it gets no `enables` block). The first-pass mapping dumped almost everything into `identity`, under-classifying the two real gameplay channels: (1) iMovement/iFlatMovement are the route's intrinsic per-plot traversal cost (consumed in CvPlot::movementCost / CvGameCoreUtils path heuristics), a `movement` world-scope modifier-family deposit, NOT identity; (2) Yields is a per-PLOT base-yield SPLIT-family deposit (food/production/commerce), added to the tile when the route is present (CvPlayer::calculatePlotRouteYieldDifference, CvPlot::calculateYield) — NOT identity. TechMovementChanges is carried in the route's XML but is an INVERSION-OUT: it is a per-TECH movement improvement (CvTeam::processTech accumulates team.getRouteChange), and curate_tech.py already folds it onto the TECH as movement.team.routes.{ROUTE}.flat — so it is DROPPED from the route's authored JSON. PrereqBonus(BonusType) + PrereqOrBonuses are prereq fields -> dropped (surface as the bonus's enables.routes). iValue (tier comparator), bSeaTunnel (water-crossing capability flag), Categories (classification trio — defined on the class but never populated for routes in XML and never read via getRouteInfo), and the unused PropertyManipulators stay in identity. iAdvancedStartCost is the advanced-start placement cost. Sole inbound boost: ImprovementInfo.RouteYieldChanges (the improvement's per-route yield bonus, applied per-plot when that improvement sits on this route) folds onto the route as a SPLIT yield family keyed by the source improvement.

ownFields.notes: Route's own per-plot traversal cost (x100 fixed-point: 100 = 1 move = MOVE_DENOMINATOR; lower = faster). Consumed in CvPlot.cpp:4528/4540 movementCost, CvGameCoreUtils.cpp:1818 path heuristic, combined at runtime with team.getRouteChange(route) (the per-tech accumulator). NOT identity (mapping mistake). 'movement' is a singleton family in FAMILY_ORDER; iMovement vs iFlatMovement need distinguishing members (cost / flatCost). OPEN: this is the route's intrinsic own-stat, arguably identity rather than a cascading pool deposit — see openQuestions.
Flat (speed-independent) movement cap: CvPlot.cpp:4540 uses max(from,to flatCost)*baseMoves, then min() against the regular cost. x100 fixed-point. Same family as iMovement, distinct member.

Route's own base-yield deposit onto the tile it occupies. CvPlayer.cpp:7692 subtracts getRouteInfo(route).getYieldChange(eYield); CvPlot calculateYield adds it when route present. SPLIT family per engine.YIELDS=[food,production,commerce] -> e.g. ROUTE_JUMPLANE = food/production/commerce .plot.flat = 1 each; ROUTE_MAGLEV = commerce.plot.flat=1. Scope is PLOT (sub-city leaf), NOT city — a route yield is a tile yield. NOT identity (mapping mistake). Zero entries dropped.

Point cost to place this route in Advanced Start (CvPlayer.cpp:17615 getAdvancedStartRouteCost). Mapping listed it under generic `cost`. Closest fine-grained costs member is the route's placement/build cost; parking as costs.world.build is tentative — see openQuestions (may warrant its own advancedStart member, mirroring Era/Handicap which parked advancedStart in identity).

Route TIER/ranking scalar (trail=1..gravityTrain=10). Used ONLY as a comparator: CvPlot.cpp:3493 (better-route check), CvPlayerAI/CvSelectionGroup best-route selection, CvUnitAI build-value weighting (iValue*..). Pure ranking, not a deposited modifier -> identity.

Boolean capability: route lets LAND units cross water tiles / blocks spurious water-route cleanup (CvPlot::isSeaTunnel, canMoveInto domain checks, build validity in CvPlayer.cpp:7574). Pure boolean flag, no scope/unit shape -> identity boolean (true emitted, false omitted). Only ROUTE_TUNNEL sets it.

getCategory/isCategory/getNumCategories trio exists on the class, but NO consumer reads them via getRouteInfo(...) anywhere in Sources/, and the <Categories> element is never populated for ANY route in CIV4RouteInfos.xml. Effectively dead on routes. Curator zero-drops the empty list, so nothing emits. Flagged for drop-confirmation in openQuestions.

m_PropertyManipulators is in getDataMembers (every Info has it) but no route in CIV4RouteInfos.xml populates it. Mirrors Improvement/Bonus curators which park PropertyManipulators in identity. Empty for all routes -> nothing emitted in practice.

INVERSION-OUT. Lives in the route's XML but is a per-TECH movement improvement: CvTeam.cpp:6068 processTech loops routes and accumulates changeRouteChange(route, getTechMovementChange(eTech)*iChange) — a team-scoped running total. mapping inversionsOut + curate_tech.py ALREADY fold it onto the TECH as movement.team.routes.{ROUTE}.flat (RouteInfo boost row in TECH_BOOSTS). So it is DROPPED from the route's own JSON. Only ROUTE_VACTRAIN sets one (TECH_SKYROADS, -4).

PREREQ field (single AND prerequisite bonus to BUILD the route): CvPlot.cpp:3505 canBuildRoute gate (isAdjacentPlotGroupConnectedBonus). Store registers RouteInfo.BonusType as an enabler edge -> surfaces as the BONUS's enables.routes, NOT on the route. Dropped from the authored route JSON (cfg.drop via mapping prereqs). Makes the route a DEPENDENT, not an enabler.

PREREQ OR-list (any one of these bonuses lets the route be built): CvPlot.cpp:3512 canBuildRoute. Store edge RouteInfo.PrereqOrBonuses/BonusType -> bonus.enables.routes. Dropped from the route JSON (top-down: lives as the bonuses' enables).
Identity-by-filename (curator writes <type>.lower().json and sets out['type']=typ). In cfg.drop as a field but re-emitted as the canonical type key.
TXT_KEY display name -> hoisted to top-level `description`.
Button .dds path -> art.icon (ART_RENAME Button->icon).
RUNTIME-only field, seeded from getSorenRand() in the constructor (NOT XML-backed). Not in getDataMembers as an XML member. Never authored -> never emitted.

inboundBoosts.notes: targetType=improvements (the TARGET key is the source improvement type). The ONLY inbound boost. An improvement carries a per-route yield bonus (m_ppiRouteYieldChanges, CvImprovementInfo::getRouteYieldChanges(route, yield)) applied to a plot when that improvement sits on a tile carrying THIS route: CvPlayer.cpp:7690 calculatePlotRouteYieldDifference, CvPlot.cpp:8230/8246/12159 calculateYield, plus AI valuation (CvPlayerAI.cpp:4903/23475, CvUnitAI.cpp:21937). mapping/ImprovementInfo.json inversionsOut RouteYieldChanges -> destEntity CvRouteInfo, shape improvementYieldChanges.{IMPROVEMENT}. Folds onto the route as SPLIT yield: <food|production|commerce>.plot.improvements.{IMPROVEMENT}.flat. SCOPE: I set plot (a per-tile route+improvement combined yield), the faithful choice — but the existing ImprovementInfo->Tech yield boosts in curate_tech.py use team/city; the boosts_config row added for routes must pick the scope. NOTE: RouteInfo.json mapping labels this boost `improvementYieldChanges` in boostsIn — same data; the family is the split yield (food/production/commerce), not a literal `improvementYieldChanges` family.

openQuestions: iMovement/iFlatMovement scope+disposition: classified as movement.world.{cost,flatCost}.flat, but these are the route's INTRINSIC own-stats (defining mechanical property), not a deposit into a cascading player/city/plot pool. They could equally be identity own-stats (like Terrain/Feature getMovementCost, which are also per-class intrinsic costs). Need an owner ruling on whether intrinsic traversal cost is a `movement` family member or identity. If movement-family, confirm the singleton family accepts members cost/flatCost (FAMILY_ORDER lists `movement` with no members today).

iAdvancedStartCost member: parked as costs.world.build, but Era/Handicap parked their advancedStart points in IDENTITY (pending review there too). Routes' advanced-start cost is a distinct per-route placement price; it may want its own costs member (e.g. advancedStart) rather than reusing `build` (which is the worker build-TIME member). Confirm against the costs fine-grained taxonomy.

Categories on RouteInfo is dead: the getCategory/isCategory trio compiles but has zero route consumers and zero XML data. Confirm it should simply be omitted (curator already zero-drops the empty list) rather than emitted as an empty identity.categories.

RouteYieldChanges inbound-boost scope: I chose `plot` (faithful — it is a per-tile yield), but the established ImprovementInfo boosts in curate_tech.py use team/city scope. Confirm the boosts_config row for RouteInfo should use plot (sub-city leaf), and that accumulate_boosts' SPLIT-family path emits member.scope.targetType.TARGET.unit = food.plot.improvements.{IMPROVEMENT}.flat as intended.

Yields scope = plot (sub-city leaf) vs city: confirmed it is a tile yield (added to the plot, not the city center), so `plot` is correct — but every other curated entity so far deposits base yields at `city`. Confirm `plot` is an accepted scope leaf in the spec's spine (world>team>empire>area>city + specialist/plot/building leaves).

result.summary: CvProcessInfo is one of the smallest Info classes in the codebase: getDataMembers (CvProcessInfo.cpp:61-67) enumerates exactly two XML-backed fields — m_iTechPrereq (enum) and m_paiProductionToCommerceModifier (commerce array) — plus the CvInfoBase base fields Type/Description/Button. A Process is a per-CITY production-conversion choice (each city may run a "Wealth/Research/Culture/Spy" process instead of building something): spent hammers convert to commerce at the per-commerce rate in ProductionToCommerceModifiers. SOURCE/SCOPE: the conversion rate is read at the city when production is spent (CvCity::changeProduction CvCity.cpp:3807-3825) — gold/espionage credited to the player total, research to the team, culture to the city — so the modifier is an intrinsic CITY-scope deposit. TechPrereq is a pure enabler gate (CvPlayer::canMaintain CvPlayer.cpp:6887 = isHasTech(prereq)); under the top-down model it is NOT authored on the Process — it inverts to the tech's `enables`/derived reverse index, so Process IS an enabler-chain member (tech -> process). NO inbound boosts exist: a repo-wide grep found no ProcessYield/ProcessCommerce/ProcessModifier field on any entity; buildings touch processes only via runtime getProductionProcess (the city's currently-selected process), never an Info field. The mapping's channel-count (commerce=city/percent, prereqs=[TechPrereq], art=[Button], identity=[Type,Description]) matches the real consumers — no under-classification here. The commerce array is a SPLIT family: it must become per-identifier families gold/research/culture/espionage (no `commerce` wrapper, no member), unit=percent (value 50 = "50% of production -> that commerce"; the consumer's /100 is percent application, NOT x100 fixed-point — values are stored as natural percents 30/40/50, so no #432 de-scaling concern here).

ownFields.family: gold/research/culture/espionage (SPLIT — per-identifier, no wrapper, no member)
ownFields.member: (none — split family; the commerce identifier IS the family name)
ownFields.notes: C2C commerce array [gold,research,culture,espionage]. Curator: split into up-to-four top-level families (gold/research/culture/espionage), shape <commerceName>.city.percent. SEMANTIC NUANCE: this is a production->commerce CONVERSION rate (production hammers turn into commerce), not a multiplier of existing commerce — see openQuestions. unit=percent (consumer multiplies by hammers then /100 at CvCity.cpp:3812-3825). Stored value is the natural percent (30/40/50), NOT x100 fixed-point, so no de-scaling. Only PROCESS_IDLE omits the field entirely (legitimate: do-nothing process).

Top-down enabler edge: the TECH enables the PROCESS (consumed only as a gate — CvPlayer::canMaintain CvPlayer.cpp:6887 isHasTech(getTechPrereq); also CvPlayerAI process-value scans 5109/5138). Under THE MODEL prereqs are NOT authored on the dependent; this inverts to the tech's `enables` + the derived reverse index (enabledByTech). DROP from the authored Process object; the store derives it. Confirms Process as an enabler-chain member.
CvInfoBase identity key (PROCESS_WEALTH, ...). The Type stem; clean, no Hungarian.
CvInfoBase TXT_KEY_ description tag; localization text channel.

CvInfoBase button art path (Art/Interface/Buttons/Process/*.dds). Per ART_RENAME the display-art reference unifies to `icon`. Process uses a DIRECT path (like tech), not an ArtDefineTag — fine for now; the future art-define alignment is a separate low-priority cleanup.

openQuestions: CONVERSION vs MULTIPLIER semantics: ProductionToCommerceModifiers is a production->commerce CONVERSION rate (hammers become commerce), not a multiplier of existing commerce like a generic commerce.percent city modifier. Folding it into the gold/research/culture/espionage families using unit=percent matches the spec's SPLIT-family vocabulary and the mapping, BUT a downstream consumer that blindly treats `gold.city.percent` as 'multiply existing gold by X%' would be WRONG here. Consider whether Process needs its own concept (e.g. a productionToCommerce conversion family/section) rather than reusing the generic commerce families. The cascade engine (#430) author should disambiguate; flagging rather than silently merging.

Destination of proceeds is split across scopes (gold/espionage -> player, research -> team, culture -> city) even though the RATE lives at the city. The flat-family model keys the modifier by where it is READ (city), which is correct for the deposit, but the per-commerce routing of the converted output is consumer behaviour not captured by scope alone. Confirm this routing is engine-side logic, not data the JSON must carry.

PROCESS_IDLE has no ProductionToCommerceModifiers and no TechPrereq — purely a do-nothing 'stop production' option. After dropping TechPrereq and (for IDLE) the absent commerce field, its authored object is just identity+text+art. Confirm an empty-modifier Process is acceptable to the store (no spurious enabler edge).

result.summary: HeritageInfo is a per-PLAYER acquired "heritage" (folklore/myth/taxon tiers). It is stored on CvPlayer::m_myHeritage, added via CvPlayer::setHeritage (driven by a unit's <Heritage> grant through CvUnit::addHeritage), and contributes EMPIRE-wide effects. Its only two real modifier-sources are EraCommerceChanges (an era-gated empire-wide commerce deposit, x100 fixed-point) and PropertyManipulators (per-player property deposits). Everything else is acquisition prerequisites (PrereqTech / PrereqOrHeritage / bNeedLanguage) that invert to derived enabler edges, plus identity/text/art. There are NO inbound modifier-boosts: no entity carries a per-Heritage modifier field (grep for Heritage{Yield,Commerce,...}Changes returns nothing). The mapping's first pass is essentially correct on channels but mislabels scope ("player" -> empire) and buries EraCommerceChanges era-keying. The runtime-only m_iMissionType is not XML-backed and is dropped.

ownFields.notes: SPLIT family: commerce -> gold/research/culture/espionage (no wrapper, no member; identifier IS the family). XML CentiCommerce is a positional 4-array (gold,research,culture,espionage) carried x100 FAITHFULLY (#432) -> named keys, never enum array. Era is a THRESHOLD CONDITION, not a scope: processHeritage (CvPlayer.cpp:30973) applies changeExtraCommerce100 for every band where currentEra >= EraType; setCurrentEra (CvPlayer.cpp:12422) recomputes via getHeritageCommerceEraChange (era==band). The deposit lands in CvPlayer::m_extraCommerce[] = a per-player/EMPIRE-wide commerce array, NOT per-city. Value is an era-keyed map: e.g. {prehistoric:{research:40,culture:10}, ancient:{research:-10,culture:10}, ...}. unit=flat (additive extra commerce). gold col is 0 in all sampled rows.

SPLIT per-PROPERTY family: each PropertySource -> its own top-level family named by PropertyType (e.g. PROPERTY_EDUCATION), no `property` wrapper, no member (owner ruling 2026-06-14; mirror curate_handicap.py lines 141-152). Consumed at the PLAYER level by CvGameObjectPlayer::foreachManipulator (CvGameObject.cpp:653) alongside civics/religion/traits/handicap -> EMPIRE scope. Sampled sources: PROPERTYSOURCE_CONSTANT -> unit perTurn, iAmountPerTurn=1, gated by an <Active><Has>{GOM_TECH:TECH_WRITING}</Has></Active> predicate. The Active/Has condition must be preserved (a gate, not dropped). Rare: only 44 of ~290 Heritages carry these (the Myths/Unicorn-style tier).

ACQUISITION PREREQ, not a modifier and not authored. Consumed ONLY in CvPlayer::canAddHeritage (CvPlayer.cpp:30919) as a hard gate (team must have the tech). Upward prereq ref -> inverts to a DERIVED top-down `enables` edge owned by the store (tech enables heritage); HeritageInfo does NOT author it. Makes HeritageInfo an enabler-chain MEMBER (tech rank -> heritage). Mapping put it under prereqs[] - correct that it is derived-not-stored on this object.

ACQUISITION PREREQ (OR over other Heritages). Consumed ONLY in CvPlayer::canAddHeritage (CvPlayer.cpp:30928): if any listed Heritage is held, this one is acquirable. Hand-written delayed-resolution vector (stays out of getDataMembers). Upward heritage->heritage prereq -> inverts to a DERIVED enabler edge (the Taxon tier requires a Folklore tier, e.g. HERITAGE_TAXON_AMPHIBIA requires HERITAGE_FOLKLORE_DART_FROG). Not authored on this object; store derives it. Confirms enabler-chain membership (heritage->heritage edges plus tech->heritage).

ACQUISITION PREREQ flag. Consumed ONLY in CvPlayer::canAddHeritage (CvPlayer.cpp:30914): if set, player must have m_bHasLanguage. Boolean prereq predicate, not a modifier -> a derived enabler-gate condition. CANDIDATE: fold into the derived prereq model as a `needsLanguage` predicate rather than author. Set on ~all Folklore-tier entries. Default false (no <bNeedLanguage>0> ever written). If kept as authored it is identity/prereq boolean (needLanguage:true), NOT any modifier family. Leaning drop->derive-into-prereq-index.
Entity identifier (HERITAGE_*). Becomes the JSON `type`/filename key.
TXT_KEY display name.
TXT_KEY pedia text reference.
Direct .dds button path (CvHotkeyInfo base supplies it). Unified to `icon` per the shared ART_RENAME convention (tech direct Button path AND bonus/building ArtDefineTag both -> icon).

RUNTIME-ONLY, NOT XML-backed: CvHeritageInfo::m_iMissionType defaults NO_MISSION and is assigned later via setMissionType (generated CvAction/CvMission wiring). Not in getDataMembers, not in the XML schema. Drop from curated JSON.

openQuestions: EraCommerceChanges shape: confirm the era-keyed map representation (era -> {commerce keys}) is the intended JSON form vs. flattening. The two consumers differ in era semantics: processHeritage uses currentEra >= band (threshold), getHeritageCommerceEraChange uses era == band (per-band delta on era transition); net effect is a per-era TOTAL extra commerce. Recommend authoring the per-era bands verbatim and letting the engine apply the threshold rule.

bNeedLanguage disposition: keep as authored identity boolean (needLanguage:true) or fold into the derived prereq/enabler index as a `needsLanguage` acquisition predicate? It is purely a canAddHeritage gate, so it belongs with the derived prereq logic, not as a standalone modifier. Decide with the prereq-model owner.

PropertyManipulators Active/Has gate: the per-source <Active><Has>{GOM_TECH:TECH_*}</Has></Active> predicate gates whether the deposit is live. Confirm how the flat-family property model expresses a conditional deposit (curate_handicap clean_property_source captures source/property/on/relation/amountPerTurn; handicap samples may be unconditional). Heritage sources ARE conditional, so the gate must be carried into the family leaf.
EraType prefix normalization: EraCommerceChanges keys are C2C_ERA_*; mirror curate_era era_fn (strip C2C_ERA_/ERA_, lowercase) when keying the era map for consistency with the era entity files.

result.summary: CvSpecialistInfo is a sub-city LEAF entity (one of specialist/plot/building) but, as a modifier SOURCE, every effect it carries deposits at CITY scope: CvCity::processSpecialist (CvCity.cpp:5130-5198) applies each field per specialist-count when a specialist is assigned to a city. result.summary: CorporationInfo is a per-city INSTITUTION source (corps spread city-to-city; effects apply in each city where the corp is active). The first-pass mapping mis-classified the four distinct commerce/yield families by lumping them all into a single flat city.commerce/city.yield, and under-classified the spread-mechanic config, maintenance, and the enabler chain. Verified against the live consumers in CvCity.cpp (calculateCorporationMaintenanceTimes100 ~7807, getCorporationYieldByCorporation ~12575, getCorporationCommerceByCorporation ~12596, updateCorporationBonus ~12681, applyCorporationModifiers ~15182), CvGame.cpp (spread/can-spread ~11163/11247/11514), and CvCity.cpp updateBuildingCommerce ~12190 (globalCorporationCommerce). FOUR separate commerce/yield families exist and must NOT be merged: (1) CommerceChanges/YieldChanges = FLAT per-city add when corp active; (2) CommercesProduced/YieldsProduced = PER-BONUS (scaled by getNumBonuses(prereqBonus) x world CorporationMaintenancePercent), a perPopulation-analog 'perBonus' unit, NOT flat; (3) HeadquarterCommerce = the HQ-revenue lever (drives per-city corp MAINTENANCE cost, corp TAX revenue, and a HQ building's globalCorporationCommerce x countCorporationLevels) — empire/world scope, NOT a per-city commerce. iMaintenance is a per-prereq-bonus maintenance rate (scaled by bonus count, world%, population). The three spread fields (iSpread influence-decay multiplier, iSpreadFactor + iSpreadCost unit-spread costs) are spread-mechanic config, not yield modifiers. BonusProduced is an enabler (free resource granted in corp cities). Prereqs (TechPrereq, ObsoleteTech, PrereqGameOption, PrereqBonuses, PrereqBuildings) + CompetingCorporations + Categories drive the derived enabler/exclusion chain — do NOT author enables/obsoletes; this entity IS an enabler-chain member. PropertyManipulators present (property family). Channel-count-isn't-POCO caveat applied: the mapping's flat-commerce channel list was wrong on semantics; trusted the C++ consumer.

result.summary: ProjectInfo is a buildable "wonder/megaproject" entity. Its modifier effects are deposited on completion by CvTeam::processProjectChange / the per-player loop in CvTeam.cpp (~4508-4576): the project sits on the building CvTeam, and its effects fan out at three distinct scopes that the first-pass mapping/ProjectInfo.json gets BACKWARDS. (1) TEAM scope: nukeInterception and techShare are team-level state (changeNukeInterception/changeTechShareCount on CvTeam). (2) EMPIRE scope (per-player-on-team, inside `player.getTeam()==getID()`): globalHappiness, globalHealth, inflationModifier, the 4 maintenance modifiers, and commerceModifier — each deposited onto EVERY player on the building team. (3) WORLD scope (every alive player game-wide, OUTSIDE the team check): worldHappiness, worldHealth, worldTradeRoutes. The mapping mis-scoped these as "team" (they are world) and lumped nuke/techShare as "player" (they are team). Project IS an enabler-chain member: store.py registers ProjectInfo.TechPrereq into the "projects" enabler index, so a tech `enables` projects (derive `enabledBy` reverse-edge; do NOT author). BonusProductionModifier is the project's OWN per-owned-bonus build-rate (CvCity::getProductionModifier 3940-3946, CvPlayer 27192-27199) — an entity-targeted cost modifier folded onto the project keyed by the bonus, NOT an inversion-out and NOT an inbound boost. NO other entity carries a per-Project change field, so inboundBoosts is EMPTY (verified: no ProjectYieldChange/ProjectCommerceChange/ProjectProductionModifier anywhere; getSpaceProductionModifier is a building's own isSpaceship-keyed field, belongs to the building). EveryoneSpecialUnit/EveryoneSpecialBuilding are one-shot makeSpecial*Valid calls = grants. The victory* fields (VictoryPrereq/Threshold/MinThreshold/DelayPercent/SuccessRate) are victory-launch mechanics consumed at team level (CvTeam getVictoryDelay/getLaunchSuccessRate, CvGame.testVictory) — real gameplay the mapping under-classified into prereqs/identity (the channel-count-isn't-POCO caveat). x100: none of these fields are x100 fixed-point (all are whole percents/counts), so #432 does not touch Project.
